sentences.text:
(Presently lodged in Central Jail, Udaipur).
----Petitioner Versus State of Rajasthan

For Respondent(s) : Mr. J.P. Bhardwaj, PP.
_____________________________________________________ HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE Judgment 06/07/2017 1. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. The petition has to be allowed for a simple reason a valuable right of the petitioner under Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 has been violated.
Exhibit P-8 is a carbon copy of the notice purported to have been sent to the petitioner by post.
No postal receipt evincing dispatch of the original to the petitioner has been proved.
No acknowledgment card establishing that the notice which was not purportedly sent was served upon the petitioner has been proved.
3. The aforesaid deficiencies have been overcome by the learned Magistrate on the reasoning that official acts are presumed to have been lawfully done.

The principle of law is (2 of 3)
[CRLR-527/1996] applicable when the doing of an act is proved.
This presumption cannot be raised with reference to sending of a notice by post.

4. In the instant case, the milk sample purchased by the Food Inspector from the petitioner was found to be adulterated on account of milk fat and milk solid not fat content being less than the prescribed percentage.
5. It is settled law that a notice under Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 is a mandatory notice to be given and proved to have been given.
'Given' means 'served' upon the accused.
The reason is a valuable right created in favour of the accused to request for a second sample to be sent to the Central Food Laboratory.
6. In the instant case, the carbon copy of the purported notice allegedly sent to the petitioner was filed along with the complaint but has not been proved.
The same is a carbon copy of the notice drawn up to be served upon the petitioner.
There are no signature of the petitioner thereon evincing service thereof upon the petitioner.

No postal receipt has been produced to evidence dispatch by Mangi Lal vs State on 6 July, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178662114/

sentences.text: No A.D. card has been proved.
7. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.

Conviction of the petitioner and sentence to undergo two years S.I. and to pay fine in sum of 500/- in the decision dated 28 th October, 1991 passed by the learned Magistrate affirmed by the Court of Sessions is set aside.
The petitioner is acquitted of the charge for having committed offence punishable under Section 6 read with Section 17 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
The bail bonds and surety bonds furnished by the petitioner on being granted by this Court are discharged.

(PRADEEP NANDRAJOG)CJ.
